Service: SAPinst - Port 21213 (Secure Installation UI over HTTPS)
Description: SAPinst is the central provisioning utility used across nearly all SAP installations, upgrades, and system migrations. When executed in secure mode, it spawns a TLS-enabled HTTP server on port 21213, offering the same installation wizard as its non-secure counterpart on port 21212 — but over HTTPS. This is intended for GUI-driven system provisioning from the localhost via a browser interface.
Deployment Context: Port 21213 is typically active only during initial provisioning phases and is not intended for exposure beyond the local machine. The interface it serves is used for a range of deployment tasks: creating new ABAP or Java instances, performing system migrations (copy/export/import workflows), configuring SIDs and hostnames, integrating database and application layers, and preparing OS-level bindings. The secure mode is usually invoked when encrypted communication is required or when custom installation automation expects HTTPS endpoints.
Access Behavior: The HTTPS listener spawned by SAPinst should only be accessible via localhost, under administrator control. Remote access — especially without enforced TLS client certificates — is a red flag indicating unsafe automation scripts, poorly hardened cloud images, or misconfigured security defaults. If port 21213 is reachable externally, it can expose the entire provisioning interface to unauthorized users, enabling abuse of installation and configuration workflows.
Functional Capabilities: Once active, this interface allows full instance provisioning: choosing the SAP product version, defining system parameters, selecting kernel packages, and connecting to supported databases (e.g. HANA, MaxDB, Oracle). It also supports platform-specific integrations like SUSE SLES hardening modules, Windows domain bindings, and OS-level scripts. If unattended installation parameters were used, sensitive info may still reside in logs or temp files.
Security Implications: From a threat perspective, this port behaves like an installation wizard with root privileges. It has been abused in pentests to replay provisioning templates, extract credentials, or execute arbitrary post-install commands via installation scripting engines. While it uses HTTPS, improper certificate validation or lack of client certificate enforcement makes the encryption superficial. Worse, old deployments often forget to kill the service post-setup, leaving behind an always-on wizard bound to an admin port.
Detection Goals: This module is intended to detect active SAPinst interfaces over HTTPS by negotiating TLS, checking the server certificate, and querying known install-related endpoints such as /sapinst. Future improvements aim to identify SAP product versions, detect leftover logs or installer artifacts, and fingerprint provisioning templates that may indicate what kind of system is being built.
Assessment Notes: If port 21213 is discovered open, it likely indicates an in-progress provisioning session or a poorly secured post-install system. Either case demands immediate review. Ensure the interface is not publicly exposed, verify it is bound only to 127.0.0.1, and terminate the service when not actively installing. The presence of this service beyond the installation window is a critical misconfiguration.
